statement: A CRITICAL production-dependency advisory blocks the Beta unless an exception below proves
it is non-applicable by a mechanically re-checkable predicate.
A HIGH production-dependency advisory blocks unless applicability can be excluded the same way.
MODERATE and LOW findings do not block by themselves; they are recorded here once reviewed so
the gate can tell a reviewed finding from a NEW one, and the gate names every unreviewed one.
A dev-only finding is out of scope for this gate, which audits the production tree only.
A scan that cannot execute is UNKNOWN. It is never PASS.
npm audit repeats one advisory on every dependent; this register lists ROOT advisories only, because the gate collapses propagation before matching.

exceptions.title: SseStream._transform() interpolates message.type and message.id into Server-Sent Events output without neutralising CR/LF
rationale: The advisory's own stated precondition is that developer code maps user-influenced data onto
the `type` or `id` fields of an SSE message: 'Direct HTTP request input does not reach these
fields without developer code bridging the gap.' This product declares no SSE surface at all,
so SseStream is never constructed and the vulnerable interpolation never executes.
The check `no-sse-surface` re-proves that mechanically on every gate run by refusing if any
@Sse() decorator, text/event-stream response or EventSource client appears in the repository.
The published fix is @nestjs/core 11.1.18, which is a NestJS 10 -> 11 major migration. Section
307 classifies a large dependency major-version migration as a product-owner decision rather
than an in-slice repair, and the finding is MODERATE, so it is recorded rather than forced.
